records.author: Hector_Lenovo
records.text:
Hi ata03!
Welcome to Lenovo Community, and thank you for describing the issue so clearly. I understand how concerning an audible high-pitched noise can be, especially when it changes at 240Hz and with different on-screen content.
Based on what you described, that behavior does not sound typical for normal use, especially if the noise is clearly noticeable from the rear of the monitor and becomes more pronounced at the native 240Hz setting. Since you have already isolated several common variables by testing a separate wall outlet and observing how brightness, HDR, and image content affect it, this may require further investigation for possible hardware inspection or warranty review.
A few practical checks you can still try:
- Test the monitor at 240Hz with a different video cable if available.
- If possible, try another power cable that is known to be compatible with your setup.
- Check whether the sound changes when the monitor is disconnected from the source device but still powered on.
- If available, test with another source device to see whether the noise behavior remains the same.
If the sound stays very faint, brief, and only happens occasionally during load changes, it is often considered normal electrical behavior /
coil whine
.
At 240Hz, does the same high‑pitched whine occur if you switch from DisplayPort 1.4 to one of the monitor’s HDMI 2.1 ports using an HDMI cable? This can help determine whether the behavior is tied more closely to the connection path or to the monitor itself.
We will be waiting for your response.
Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

records.source_title: 11-24-2026 08:06:18 Lenovo Legion 24-15 – High-Pitched Coil Whine at 240Hz (Color/Load Dependent) byata03inY Gaming Accessories & Curved Gaming Monitors Hello Lenovo Support Team, I recently purchased a Lenovo Legion 24-15 monitor, and I am experiencing>Here are my specific findings after troublesho
records.author: ata03
records.text:
Hello Lenovo Support Team,
I recently purchased a Lenovo Legion 24-15 monitor, and I am experiencing an audible high-pitched coil whine coming from the rear of the unit (near the power and DisplayPort input area) when running at its native 240Hz refresh rate.
Here are my specific findings after troubleshooting:
Refresh Rate Dependency: At 144Hz, the monitor is relatively silent. However, switching to 240Hz produces a noticeable high-pitched whine that is audible from a normal seating distance in a quiet room.
Color/Panel Load Pattern: At 240Hz, fullscreen pure black screens produce relatively little noise, whereas fullscreen solid RGB colors (Red, Green, or Blue) and bright/colorful desktop content immediately trigger and amplify the whine.
Setup & Verification: Tested via DisplayPort 1.4 and directly connected to a separate wall outlet. Adjusting brightness and disabling HDR slightly reduces the intensity, but the issue persists at 240Hz.
Could you please confirm whether this level of coil whine at 240Hz is considered within normal operating specifications for the Legion 24-15, or if it qualifies for a hardware inspection/replacement under warranty?
Thank you for your assistance.

records.author: Lorenzo_Lenovo

Hello Selte,
Welcome to Lenovo Community
I understand your concern with the
ThinkVision P40WD-40

Since you’ve already tried several good steps, here are some additional procedures that you can try:
1) Open the monitor’s on-screen menu and check whether the brightness/color difference is visible there as well.
2) In macOS Display settings, test the affected scaled resolutions again and compare them with the Default option.

To help narrow this down, When the issue happens, does the same left/right split or color distortion appear in the monitor’s built-in OSD menu (the on-screen monitor settings menu)? This helps determine whether the issue is happening within the monitor itself or only with the video signal from the MacBook.
Let me know how things go.

records.source_title: 11-14-2026 20:34:34 ThinkVision P40WD-40 – split brightness/color display with macOS scaling and color errors bySelteinDisplays, Options and Accessories Good day, I am using a new Lenovo ThinkVision P40WD-40 with a new 14-inch MacBook Pro withDifferent display of the two halves of the screen At cert
records.author: Selte
records.text:
Good day,
I am using a new Lenovo ThinkVision P40WD-40 with a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 processor. Two display issues occur:
1. Different display of the two halves of the screen
At certain scaled resolutions, the monitor shows an exactly centered split: the two halves of the screen differ significantly in brightness or color saturation.
With the macOS setting “Default,” the split disappears.
It reappears as soon as I switch to the next higher scaling setting at 3200 × 1350.
The behavior occurs both via a direct HDMI connection and via the included Lenovo Thunderbolt 4 cable.
With HDR enabled, the left half sometimes appears heavily oversaturated, while the right half displays significantly paler colors.
2. Severe color distortions via Thunderbolt with HDR disabled
With the included Thunderbolt 4 cable, severe color distortions occur when HDR is turned off. App icons and images in PowerPoint show colorful color fringing, jagged edges, and distorted areas of color.
With HDR enabled, these artifacts largely disappear, but the colors appear excessively vivid. Correct color display was possible via HDMI; however, the scaling-dependent split described in point 1 also occurs there.
The errors are clearly visible in photos taken with the iPhone. Screenshots generated by the Mac, on the other hand, do not show the anomalies in the same way.
Measures already taken
Reset the monitor to factory settings
Completely disconnected the monitor from power and turned it back on
Tested different Thunderbolt ports on the MacBook
Tested a direct HDMI connection for comparison
Reduced the refresh rate to 60 Hz
Tested different scaling settings as well as HDR on/off
Checked the monitor color modes and macOS color profile
Updated macOS
The measures have not permanently resolved the issues. However, switching back to “Default” reliably eliminates the centered split—both via HDMI and via Thunderbolt.
Thank you very much for your support.
Kind regards, Andreas
